prs.title: Agents are stopped from working under an old copy of AGENTS.md, and told when a new version goes live
prs.body:
## In plain English
**What changes:** Every agent now checks, before it claims or takes over files, commits or pushes, that the AGENTS.md it is reading is the same one origin/main has right now. If its copy is older, it is stopped with one clear line: "STALE_POLICY: your AGENTS.md is 25.0.1, origin/main is 26.0.0; work from fresh origin/main (scripts/new-worktree.sh) and re-read §0". CI fails a PR built under an older policy. When a new version (27, 28, …) reaches main, every open claim on the board is flagged "policy changed" and you get one Telegram line per version: "AGENTS.md 27.0.0 is live; N open claims were on 26.0.0 and have been told".
**Why:** Your question on 2026-10-28: "How can we force every agent to, before they start, to look at the latest copy of the agents.md and not a cache copy? This is critical … How about if we go to [version] 27? How do the agents automatically know to check in to see if there's a new one?" Until now nothing checked. Measured today: this machine's main checkout still held AGENTS.md 25.0.1 while origin/main had 26.0.0, and nothing noticed. The new check reports it as STALE.
**Who / what it affects:** All agents (Claude, Codex, Cursor) in their own worktrees. A stale agent is refused at `agent_claim.py claim/next/take` and `takeover --claim`, at `git commit` and at `git push`, and its PR fails `agent-governance`. Agents already mid-task see "POLICY CHANGED" in `agent_claim.py status`. You see at most one Telegram line per new AGENTS.md version and nothing else. Nothing changes for trading, the broker, the Command Center pages or any schedule.
**When it takes effect:** After merge, for every worktree and branch made from main from then on: hooks, CI and the claim tool run from the branch's own copy. Branches made before the merge keep their old hooks until they are rebased. The Telegram broadcast runs inside the existing deploy-on-main timer. Its first run only records today's version as a baseline, so you get no message for 26.0.0. The first message comes with the next version.
**Approval:** Held, operator's own merge. It touches `.githooks/pre-push`, `scripts/agent_claim_precommit.sh`, `scripts/deploy_on_main_poll.py` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`, which are held classes in §25.10.
**Risk and fallback:** False refusals are the main risk. If GitHub is unreachable, the check compares against the last fetch and says so. If it cannot compare at all, it prints a loud UNKNOWN warning and lets work continue, so it never blocks offline work silently and never passes silently. A branch that raises the AGENTS.md version on top of main is recognised as ahead, not stale. One that lowers it is refused. We would notice through refusals in agent output or an unexpected Telegram line. To undo it, revert this PR. Nothing switches the check off. The existing claim override (`TRADEAI_CLAIM_OVERRIDE`) skips only the separate file-ownership check, which runs after this one passes. The fetch timeout cannot be set below 3 seconds, so nobody can use it to fake offline mode. The test-only skip works only inside the test runner. The fix for a refusal is always a rebase or a fresh worktree.

## Technical detail
- Base SHA: `e2e699517fbf18ce7f66f464deb3087b80cbb928` · Head SHA: `e2eb2fc574850f24368030ae3b09fa4cd7aefaa7` (commits `b1f4347de` feature, `957e83bbd` shard duration hints, `e2eb2fc57` review fixes)
- Claim id and worktree: `20261028T144853Z-claude-7d9d98be`, `<host-path-redacted>`, branch `feat/policy-freshness-gates-20261028`. Claiming `.github/pull_request_template.md` automatically recorded a takeover of stale claim `20261028T020849Z-claude-948c6521`. That is the 26.0.0 docs claim, whose PR #2256 is merged.
- Files and named stores changed:
  - `scripts/lib/policy_freshness.py` (new). It is the one shared check. It runs `git fetch origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main` with a timeout (`TRADEAI_POLICY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S`, default 6 s), compares blob ids (the worktree file, or `<rev>:AGENTS.md` for pushed commits) with `origin/main:AGENTS.md`, and parses both `Policy-Version`s. It returns `OK` / `STALE` / `UNKNOWN`, with exit codes 0 / 1 / 3. Offline it falls back to the last fetch and reports the time. A branch is exempt only when its merge-base with origin/main already holds main's AGENTS.md blob AND its Policy-Version is not lower than main's (a lower or unreadable version is STALE). The fetch timeout has a 3 s floor. It never raises.
  - `scripts/agent_claim.py`: `claim`, `claim --add`, `next`, `take` and `takeover --claim` refuse STALE. Every claim records `policy_version`, `policy_blob` and `policy_check`, and `heartbeat` refreshes them. `status` prints `POLICY CHANGED`. The import is lazy, so a copied hook tree without the library warns instead of crashing. The claim-board suites skip the gate only through the in-process module attribute `RUN_POLICY_GATE_UNDER_PYTEST`, and only while pytest is running a test. No environment variable or flag can turn the gate off.
  - `scripts/lib/agent_claim_board.py`: `claim(policy=…)` and `heartbeat(policy=…)`. A new sidecar `<claims_dir>/policy_changed/<claim_id>.json` (`AgentClaimPolicyChanged@v1`) records the mark, because the claim file stays its owner's alone. Board rows gain `policy_version`, `policy_blob` and `policy_changed`.
  - `scripts/agent_claim_precommit.sh`: the freshness check runs before the claim check. STALE exits 1, while UNKNOWN or a missing library warns.
  - `.githooks/pre-push`: checks every pushed commit after authorization and budget are decided, and before the secrets scan, grant consumption and budget recording. A refused push therefore costs no grant use and no budget count.
  - `scripts/check_agents_policy_state.py` adds rule 6, which the `agent-governance` workflow already runs. A PR fails when its head Policy-Version is behind the `origin/$GITHUB_BASE_REF` tip, including when the PR itself changed the version to a lower one (a downgrade is never a bump). An unparseable Policy-Version on either side fails with `UNKNOWN_POLICY`.
  - `scripts/lib/policy_version_broadcast.py` (new), called from `scripts/deploy_on_main_poll.py` after each poll. It is a dry run unless the call is the host timer's `--apply` without `--dry-run`, it is skipped when the fetch failed, and it never changes the poll's outcome. On a new version it marks open claims and calls `send_system(text, identity="policy-version-live:<v>", kind="policy_version_live")`. An undelivered line is retried, at most 6 sends per version. State is kept in `<claims_dir>/policy_broadcast_state.json` (`PolicyBroadcastState@v1`).
  - `scripts/agent_session_start.sh`: prints the freshness line first, with a STALE banner. It stays advisory and always exits 0.
  - Docs: `docs/ops/AGENT_CLAIM_BOARD.md` §16, `docs/ops/AGENT_START_HERE.md`, and the Cursor start rule `docs/ops/agent_start/cursor-rule.md` (step 0).
  - `.github/pull_request_template.md`: a checklist for PRs that change AGENTS.md, including "After merge: update the claude.ai Project copy of AGENTS.md".
- Contracts changed: `AgentClaim@v1` gains optional `policy_version`, `policy_blob` and `policy_check` (additive). New: `PolicyFreshness@v1`, `AgentClaimPolicyChanged@v1`, `PolicyBroadcastState@v1`, `PolicyBroadcastRun@v1`.
- Migrations: none.
- Session-start hook placement: the repo has no tracked `.claude/settings.json`. `.gitignore` keeps `.claude/*` untracked apart from `skills/`. The existing convention is the operator-installed `scripts/agent_session_start.sh` (SessionStart in `~/.claude/settings.json`), so this PR extends that script and adds no settings file. For Cursor, the existing mechanism is the start rule snippet, so step 0 was added there. `.cursor/hooks.json` points at absolute paths in the guardrails worktree and was left alone.
- Tests run (command and result), including negative / refusal tests:
  - `pytest tests/test_policy_freshness_20261028.py tests/test_policy_freshness_gates_20261028.py` → 54 passed. Covered: OK, STALE (fetch reveals a moved main; versions are never hard-coded), same version with different text, an exempt bump branch (committed and uncommitted), a bump built on an old main (STALE), UNKNOWN (no origin, no repo, no AGENTS.md), offline (STALE still refuses, OK is labelled), fetch timeout, and CLI exit codes. Each gate is tested end to end for OK, STALE, exempt, UNKNOWN and offline: claim, claim --add, next, real `pre-commit` and `pre-push` subprocesses (no budget charged on refusal; authorization still checked first), CI rule 6 (unit and end to end), session start, the poller hook (dry unless `--apply`; skipped on fetch failure; never raises), the broadcast (baseline, dry run writes nothing, marks plus one send, per-version dedupe, bounded retry), the `status` row clearing after a heartbeat, takeover gated and recording the policy, a downgrade on top of main (STALE), an equal-version edit on top of main (exempt), an unreadable version on an edit branch (STALE), CI rule 6 failing on a downgrade and on an unparseable version, the 3 s fetch-timeout floor, a real CLI process with `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` and the old skip variables set still refusing, and `TRADEAI_CLAIM_OVERRIDE` not bypassing a STALE commit.
  - Existing suites → 572 passed together with the two new files (re-run after the review fixes): the claim board (board, lifecycle, merge paths, shared paths, worklog, task board, evidence-only, work board and pipeline), hooks (`test_ai_work_policy_hooks.py`, `test_agent_hooks_ci_hermetic.py`), governance (`test_agents_policy_v1.py`, 20.0.0, 20.3.0, 25.0.0, 26.0.0, `test_pr_plain_english_20261027.py`), deploy-on-main (3 files), and the remaining agent-governance workflow tests.
  - `check_test_coverage.py --fail-on-new` ok. `check_test_host_paths.py --fail-on-new` → 0 new violations. `check_line_endings.py --range origin/main` → none. `agent_changed_file_quality.py --paths <all changed>` passes, with ruff 0.16.2 check and format; `agent_claim.py` and `check_agents_policy_state.py` carried pre-existing format drift and are now formatted. `report_docs_inventory.py --check-index` PASS, with no regeneration needed. `validate_sop_evidence_integrity.py` ok. `check_agents_policy_state.py --base origin/main` ok. shellcheck is clean on the three shell files.
- Dry run (§0 rule 7), `scripts/lib/policy_version_broadcast.py --dry-run` against the live board: `"action": "baseline", "mode": "dry_run", "version": "26.0.0", "marked": [], "telegram": null`. On a copy of the board with a seeded 25.0.1 state it returned `"action": "broadcast"`, 12 claims to mark, and text `AGENTS.md 26.0.0 is live; 12 open claims were on 25.0.1 and have been told`, with nothing written or sent.
- Shard duration hints: added in `957e83bbd` under the `supplement_20261028` note (`tests/test_policy_freshness_20261028.py` 3.8 s, `tests/test_policy_freshness_gates_20261028.py` 9.7 s). The review fixes added no new test files. Re-measured after the fixes: 3.7 s and 10.2 s, close enough that the hints stand.
- Proof after release (what will be checked on CURRENT, and how): `python3 scripts/lib/policy_freshness.py --gate session` in a fresh worktree prints `policy OK: AGENTS.md 26.0.0 matches origin/main`. The deploy poller receipt (`--json`) carries `policy_broadcast.action == "baseline"` once, then `"none"`, and `policy_broadcast_state.json` exists in the claims dir. A claim made afterwards carries `policy_version` and `policy_blob`.

## Independent review
The independent review (a reviewer other than this author's session) returned **CHANGES**. Each finding was fixed in `e2eb2fc57`, with tests:
1. MEDIUM: `takeover --claim` was not gated. It now runs the same freshness gate and records the policy fields.
2. MEDIUM: the exemption allowed a downgrade (it only checked that the merge-base held main's copy). A lower or unreadable Policy-Version on such a branch is now STALE. CI rule 6 fails a lower head version even when the PR changed it.
3. LOW: the test skip could be set from outside through an environment variable, and a tiny `TRADEAI_POLICY_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S` could force offline mode. The skip is now an in-process module attribute that only works while pytest runs a test, and the timeout has a 3 s floor.
4. LOW: an unparseable Policy-Version passed CI rule 6. It now fails with `UNKNOWN_POLICY`.
5. LOW: the `.githooks/pre-push` header comment did not mention the gate. It now does.
6. PR body: head SHA updated, the duration-hints blocker removed (done in `957e83bbd`), the override statement corrected, and this section added.

Re-review of `e2eb2fc57` by the same read-only reviewer: **MERGE**. All six fixed; 54/54 tests in the two new files pass; rule 6 checked directly on downgrade (fails), bump (passes), same version (passes), unparseable (fails), no base (skipped). Remaining Low notes, accepted: an agent that deliberately runs the CLI inside a pytest-loaded Python process with `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` set still skips the gate (needs intent, not an accident); rule 6 fails every PR if main's AGENTS.md ever loses a readable Policy-Version (fails safe).

Adversarial-review: CHANGES (2 Medium, 4 Low) → all fixed in e2eb2fc57 → re-review MERGE (independent read-only reviewer).

### Proposed AGENTS.md §28 rule (for the separate, versioned held change; not edited here)

> ## 28.17 Work under the current AGENTS.md
>
> - **An agent works only under the AGENTS.md that origin/main holds now.** Before it claims, commits or pushes, it
>   runs (or its hooks run) `scripts/lib/policy_freshness.py`, which fetches origin/main and compares blob ids. A
>   `STALE_POLICY` refusal means: stop, work from fresh origin/main (`scripts/new-worktree.sh`), re-read §0, then
>   continue. A branch that edits AGENTS.md on top of main's current copy, with a version not lower than main's, is not
>   stale. `UNKNOWN` is a warning, never a pass. Nothing overrides STALE: the fix is a rebase or a fresh worktree. *Cause: 2026-10-28 — the canonical checkout
>   still held 25.0.1 a day after 26.0.0 was ratified, and nothing noticed (LESSONS L28-29).*
> - **A version change reaches agents mid-task.** When a new Policy-Version reaches main, every open claim is marked
>   `policy_changed` and `agent_claim.py status` shows it; the agent re-reads AGENTS.md, rebases, and heartbeats from
>   the fresh worktree to clear it. The operator gets one Telegram line per version. CI fails a PR whose AGENTS.md
>   version is behind its base. *Cause: 2026-10-28 — operator: "How do the agents automatically know to check in to
>   see if there's a new one?" (LESSONS L28-29).*
> - **After an AGENTS.md change merges, the claude.ai Project copy is updated** (PR template checklist). *Cause:
>   2026-10-28 — agents outside the repo read that copy (LESSONS L28-29).*

prs.title: [shared-infra] Operator resume settles an idle deploy STOP itself now that no controller exists
prs.body:
## In plain English

- **What changes:** After a deploy STOP, the operator's `resume` command now works on its own. If no deploy is running, `resume` itself completes the "STOP has settled" step (the step the retired release-train controller used to do), writes down that the operator did it, and resumes. Messages now say "deploy STOP" instead of "release train STOP".
- **Why:** The controller that settled a STOP was retired on 2026-10-27, so every `resume` after a `stop` was refused (STOP_NOT_SETTLED). Today the operator had to run two internal library calls by hand, pretending to be the controller, before `resume` worked.
- **Who / what it affects:** Only the operator's host command `scripts/release_control_cli.py resume` and its library `scripts/lib/release_control.py`. The deploy poller, the emergency promote and Ops -> Controls resume behave as before (one difference: a resume refused as STOP_NOT_SETTLED now also writes a journal row, from any caller). No trading, broker or order code is touched.
- **When it takes effect:** On the first deploy after merge; it only matters the next time the operator runs `stop` and then `resume`.
- **Approval:** Held for the operator's own merge (held class `merge_deploy_control`; shared-infra). Needs two independent review receipts first (AGENTS.md §28.15 item 3).
- **Risk and fallback:** The rule "do not resume while something is in flight" is kept: `resume` settles only while it holds the same global release lock the deploy poller holds for a whole deploy; if a deploy holds it, `resume` still refuses. The typed phrase (`RESUME EPOCH n`) at a real terminal is still required. We would notice a problem as a `resume` that refuses or a settle row in `control_journal.jsonl` we did not expect. Fallback: revert this PR; the manual acknowledge + settle steps keep working unchanged.

## Technical detail

- `ReleaseControl.resume(..., settle_if_idle=False)` gains an opt-in. With `True` and mode in STOP_REQUESTED / STOP_ACKNOWLEDGED / SETTLING: operator proof is verified first (unchanged), then `GlobalReleaseLock(state_dir, timeout_s=0)` is taken. Busy -> journal `resume` REFUSED `STOP_NOT_SETTLED` with `in_flight: true`, nothing else written. Acquired -> `_settle_idle_held` sets mode STOPPED, fills acknowledged/settling/stopped timestamps, writes `stop.settled_by` {actor, via: resume, from_mode, in_flight: false, signal}, journals `operator_settle` under the operator's actor, then the normal resume runs (prior stop kept in `resumed.prior_stop`) and the lock is released.
- In-flight signal: `<state_dir>/.lock`, held by `deploy_on_main.poll_once` across prepare, promote and post_release_tester. Known gap: `scripts/emergency_manual_promote.sh` only probes this lock and does not hold it during its prepare/promote, so an emergency promote started before the STOP is not visible to this check. It refuses to start while STOP is latched, and both it and `resume` are run by hand by the operator.
- The CLI passes `settle_if_idle=True`. `scripts/lib/ops_controls_core.py` (passkey applier) does not opt in and still answers STOP_NOT_SETTLED; changing it is a separate held change.
- Wording: STOP latch `detail` and CLI help say "deploy STOP". No API renamed.
- Tests: new `tests/test_release_control_resume_settle_20261028.py` (12 pass): CLI stop -> resume with nothing in flight; refusal with the lock held (all three unsettled phases, library and CLI); default refusal without opt-in; audit records who settled; no settle row when already STOPPED; wrong phrase settles nothing; wording. Gate: `config/ci_gates/release_control_resume_settle_20261028.json`. Related suites (release_train_authority, ops_controls_sudo_window, deploy_on_main_autonomy, release_grant_capability_binding, agents_policy 17/19/22, ops_controls) 424 passed, 1 skipped. ruff check and format clean.
- Shard duration hint NOT added: `config/ci_shard_duration_hints.json` is claimed by the live policy-freshness claim. Add `"tests/test_release_control_resume_settle_20261028.py": 1.7` (local one-file wall clock) when it is released. Not required: the duration-hint coverage test passes without it (7/7).
- Held class (`scripts/lib/merge_hold_paths.py` held_classes): `merge_deploy_control` for `scripts/lib/release_control.py`. Shared-infra (`scripts/check_shared_infra_pr.py` MINIMUM `scripts/*release*.py`, `scripts/lib/release*.py`): `scripts/release_control_cli.py`, `scripts/lib/release_control.py`; the title must start `[shared-infra] `.

Real-layout proof: scratch state dir, armed, `release_control_cli.py stop`, then `resume` under a real pty (`script -qec`) typing `RESUME EPOCH 3` -> `RESUMED`, epoch 3, `settled_by.actor.kind=host_cli`, status mode RUNNING latch ABSENT, one `operator_settle` journal row, latch archived to `windows/STOP-20261028T151324Z.json.archived`.

## Independent review
A read-only reviewer that did not write this change: **MERGE**. Checked that the deploy poller holds the same lock for the whole deploy (`scripts/lib/deploy_on_main.py:546-575`) and systemd kills its children on timeout, so resume can't settle while a deploy runs; the lock is released in `finally`; locks are taken in one order (no deadlock); the typed phrase is checked before any lock or write; the audit rows name `host_cli`. Low notes: the emergency promote script doesn't hold the lock during its own promote (pre-existing, stated above); the refusal journal row (now stated above).

Adversarial-review: MERGE (independent read-only reviewer, 1c7861fad); 2 Low, documented.
